title: Curated route+model lineage factset for Console cost & latency attribution
creator: Maya Chen
description: Create a curated set of fact tables that attribute Console API cost and latency to the combination of route (API endpoint) and model variant (including quantization/profile). The goal is to enable per-route, per-model unit economics and latency SLO dashboards, support rollback/rollout analysis, and feed Redwood Optimize recommendations. This ticket covers the schema design, dbt models, materialized tables, backfill approach, and QA tests. Grain: one record per minute per route+model+workspace with aggregated counters and distribution sketches for latency and token counts. We will join to existing workspace, route, and model dimension tables and preserve model lineage (model_id, model_version, quantization_profile, runtime_variant).
tasks: Design schema and finalize grain + partition strategy (minute-level grain, partition by day)
Add model_lineage_dim to capture model_version, variant, quant_profile and deploy_id
Implement dbt incremental model for route_model_minute_fact with idempotent upsert logic
Create latency histogram using t-digest sketches and token count distribution buckets
Wire cost attribution calculations using token pricing and model unit-cost lookup
Add dbt tests: uniqueness on (minute,route_id,model_id,workspace_id), not_null for cost and event_count
Backfill plan and run: 90-day rolling backfill in 7-day windows with checkpointing
Hook new factset into Console dashboards and create initial slices for top routes and high-cost workspaces
Create monitoring alerts for data freshness, row-count regressions, and drift in average latency
acceptance_criteria: route_model_minute_fact materialized and incrementally populated for last 7 days in production dataset
dbt run produces no fresh test failures and all new tests pass in CI
Backfill completed for a 30-day pilot window without data duplication and with validation run against raw event counts
Console dashboard has a working slice that shows cost per 1M tokens by route and model variant
SMOKE queries for top-10 high-cost routes return within SLA (<2s) using the new curated tables

notes: Design choices: use minute-level grain to balance queryability vs storage. Use t-digest sketches for p95/p99 latency instead of storing raw lists. Cost attribution joins tokens emitted to model pricing table; for cached responses mark cost as zero and set cache_hit flag. Backfill should be staged to a temporary dataset and validated with reconciliation queries before swapping into curated namespace. Plan to run smoke aggregate reconciliation daily for first two weeks post-release.
